title: ArcaneDispatch Policy
description: Shared schema for the policy.json the Dart container app writes to the App Group container and the macOS Network Extension reads on startTunnel / reloadPolicy. Authoritative source — both lib/core/policy.dart and macos/ArcaneDispatchTunnel/Engine/PolicyStore.swift MUST stay aligned with this document. Bump `version` and the schemaVersion constants in lockstep when fields are added or removed in a breaking way.

version.description: Wire-schema version. Mirrors Policy.schemaVersion in Dart and the matching constant in Swift. Extensions that see a higher version than they understand MUST refuse to start and surface a `failed` status.

mode.description: Active bonding mode. Maps to BondingMode in Dart and the scheduler choice in the extension.

killSwitch.description: When true, the transport blocks egress whenever the supervisor reports no healthy link. The extension MUST drop packets rather than fall through to the kernel's default route.

dnsServers.description: DNS servers the tunnel announces via NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings.dnsSettings. Empty falls back to system defaults.

splitTunnelAllowList.description: Hostnames / suffixes that bypass the tunnel. Implemented as suffix match in the extension. Empty means everything goes through the tunnel.

serverUrl.description: Relay URL (e.g. udp://relay.example.com:4430). Null means no relay is configured yet.

serverToken.description: Opaque per-client auth token issued by the server's genkey/adduser commands. Stored in the App Group for the extension to read.

bondedTransport.description: When true, the macOS Network Extension sends packet flow through the relay-backed bonded transport.

captivePortalAssist.description: When true, the container app's CaptivePortalDetector runs per-link probes against http://captive.apple.com/ and demotes captive links to Backup until they pass. The extension itself doesn't probe — it only reacts to the priorities Dart pushes into policy.json.

links.description: All configured uplinks in user-defined order. UI ordering and dispatcher ordering both consume this list as-is.

id.description: Stable identifier (typically `legacy:<token>` or a generated UUID). Used as the join key for metrics and the App Group shared state. MUST be unique across links.

label.description: Human display name. Defaults to the interface name in Dart.

interfaceName.description: Optional system interface name (e.g. en0). When null, sourceAddress alone is used; at least one of these must resolve to a usable source IP.

sourceAddress.description: Literal source IP or CIDR override. Free-form because we need both v4 and v6.

priority.description: Routing bucket. Engine tries primary first while any primary is healthy, then secondary, then backup. `never` is excluded entirely.

weight.description: Integer weight inside the priority bucket. Maps onto the legacy `<target>/<weight>` syntax. Used by the weighted round-robin dispatcher.

speedCapBps.description: Per-link throughput cap in bytes/second. Null = no cap. Enforced by the token-bucket limiter on each engine instance.

dataCapBytes.description: Per-billing-cycle data allowance in bytes. Null = no cap. When dataUsedBytes >= dataCapBytes the supervisor marks the link as disabled.

dataUsedBytes.description: Running counter incremented by the data meter. Resets on billingCycleAnchor rollover.

billingCycleAnchor.description: ISO-8601 date string used as the monthly rollover anchor for dataUsedBytes.

status.description: Last-known health state, written by the supervisor. Persisted so the UI can show a meaningful state on cold boot. The extension MUST ignore this field — the running supervisor is the only writer.
